answer: A new agent may vote only after three established peers each lock a distinct bond in a shared time-locked vault for two checkpoints, and those same peers cannot vouch for anyone else that epoch. If a later funding-graph check shows the applicant and its sponsors share a wallet cluster, all four bonds are slashed to the challengers. Voting rights then ripple out at one new ballot per checkpoint, so a purchased farm cannot suddenly fill the meadow of open seats in a single block. The gate is the delayed bond plus the vouch cap, not a display name.
